messages:
sarah: heads-up — canary fleet started throwing OOMs ~15m after the kernel-routing + shadow-allocator merge. blocking rollout :eyes:
jia: ugh. which shard/region? any repro on staging?
sarah: us-west-2 canaries (pool-id rwd-canary-7). repro on a box with longctx load. attaching kernel logs and a short pprof snippet:
```
OOM killed process 4123 (runtime) total-vm: 18G, anon-rss: 11G
kv_cache: allocated 9.8G, fragmentation: 32% 
stack: runtime.newstack+0x...
```
kevin: CI perf job also flagged memory regression in the same commit range — buildkite/1234 shows +27% RSS on the longctx perf suite. commit: 9f3b2a7 (kernel-router: prefer-quantfast; shadow-allocator: enable compaction)
omar: can you paste the allocator metrics? shadow-allocator has compaction phases that run async — maybe compaction is thrashing with autobatch?
sarah: here's dump from /metrics on the failing host:
```
kv_alloc_count: 1_234_567
kv_free_count: 1_129_001
kv_compact_cycles: 432
kv_compact_time_ms: 51234
kv_fragmentation_pct: 31.8
inflight_batches: avg 42, p95 210
```
jia: fragmentation ~32% + high inflight_batches at p95 = suspicious. Could be a race between batched handoff and compaction pauses.
kevin: timeline: deploy at 10:12 -> first OOM at 10:27 -> compaction spikes at 10:26 in metrics. matches.
sarah: repro script to run locally (small):
```
# emulate longctx tail workload
python tools/run_longctx_load.py --seq-dist heavy --qps 180 --duration 600 --trace-profile
```
omar: running now on a canary spare. if we can get a heap profile during the compaction spike that'd help. jia, can you instrument kv allocator to dump freelist sizes on compaction start?
jia: will add lightweight logging, but prefer toggling shadow-allocator.compaction=false to validate. can someone flip config in canary?
kevin: toggled: shadow-allocator.compaction=false on pool rwd-canary-7 via rollout UI at 10:45. watching.
sarah: immediate drop in compaction_time_ms and fragmentation stabilizing. no new OOMs for 12m. looks like compaction is the trigger when inflight batch pressure is high.
omar: hypothesis: compaction tries to coalesce small slabs while autobatch/hand-off is creating new tiny allocations, leading to fragmentation spikes and ephemeral RSS growth -> kernel router picks quantfast kernels that assume contiguous allocations and blow up GC/kmap pressure.
kevin: needs bisect. candidate PRs: #5423 (kernel-router preferences) and #5481 (shadow-allocator compaction heuristics). both merged ~10:00. which to revert?
sarah: revert compaction heuristic first (safer), keep kernel-routing disabled until we confirm.
kevin: rolling revert of #5481 to canary now. buildkite-bot: revert pr/5481 merged by kevin at 11:02 (sha: 3b7c4d).
sarah: canary running reverted build — sending load.
omar: initial signs look good. fragmentation down to 12% after 8m, compaction cycles zero.
jia: plan: 1) keep revert for rollout hold 2) add compaction back with stronger backoff under high inflight_batch pressure 3) run kerner-router change behind a feature flag with quantfast disabled for now 4) add allocator freelist size histograms to CI perf longctx job
kevin: agree. I'll open followups. tagging eng-oncall for monitoring. rollout blocked until followups merged and validated. :thumbsup:
buildkite-bot: perf/longctx job #1245: baseline vs current RSS diff: +2% after revert (within noise).
sarah: thanks team — filing postmortem notes and followups. assigning jia and kevin to PRs.
